category.name: Application hosting and backends
category.description: Deployment platforms and backend services for business web and mobile applications.
category.audience: Software teams and businesses building their own applications
category.audienceRationale: Relevant across industries but directly used by software delivery teams rather than every employee.

pricing.note: Basic always-on dyno $7/month; Eco $5/month sleeps and personal accounts only; databases and add-ons extra.
Pro developer seat $20/month plus metered services; Hobby free plan separate.
Blaze pay-as-you-go per service after applicable free quotas; no single monthly entry price.

oss.name: Coolify
oss.classificationReason: Pricing explicitly grants all self-hosted features with no restrictions; cloud fee buys managed control-plane hosting, not application server capacity.

oss.name: PocketBase
oss.classificationReason: MIT volunteer project; FAQ confirms no commercial organization or vendor hosting. Technical single-server/SQLite limits are architecture, not paid feature gates.

locked: Premium Enterprise self-hosted edition: console SSO, custom organization roles, activity logs, advanced management tools and compliance options
oss.classificationReason: BSD-3-Clause core self-hosts auth, database, storage, functions and realtime. Enterprise page explicitly reserves premium self-hosted management capabilities. General guide parity language is broader, so exact edition boundary merits continued checking.

locked: Dokku Pro JSON API and HTTP(S) Git push
oss.classificationReason: MIT core deploys Heroku-compatible apps through Git and CLI. Paid self-hosted Pro add-on supplies everyday graphical administration and API/HTTP push; Pro is explicitly not hosting.

oss.name: Supabase self-hosted stack
oss.classificationReason: Apache-2.0 self-hosted Postgres/auth/storage/realtime stack has no documented paid self-hosted code tier. A applies to this named OSS backend stack. Managed-platform services and control-plane gaps are separately disclosed; it is a partial Firebase alternative, not an equivalent managed platform.

health.rsx: Central authenticated rsx analysis available; overall score 7.2/10. Not used as edition/licensing proof.

serviceLimitations: Managed cloud branching, Management API, managed backups/PITR, advanced platform metrics, analytics/vector buckets and ETL are absent from the self-hosted distribution; no paid self-hosted unlock is claimed. Operate backups, monitoring and deployment workflows yourself or use managed cloud.

alternatives.migrationNotes: Git/container app deployment on your own servers; move environment variables, domains and databases; operate backups, security and scaling yourself. Heroku add-ons need replacements.
Deploy web apps and static sites to owned infrastructure; Vercel edge/CDN, serverless integrations and managed observability require separate infrastructure or adaptation.
Supports Heroku-compatible apps/buildpacks and git push, but owner operates host and datastores; audit buildpack/plugin compatibility, migrate add-on data and configure backups.
Postgres relational backend with auth, realtime and storage; rewrite Firebase SDK calls, security rules and document data into SQL schemas; self-hosting requires production operations.

Backend auth, databases, files, functions and realtime overlap; replace Firebase SDKs, migrate users/data and reimplement security/permissions. Firebase analytics and mobile services require separate evaluation.
Small single-server auth/realtime/file backend using SQLite; no Cloud Functions and vertical scaling only. Rewrite client calls and rules; FAQ reports no built-in data import/export helpers.

uncertainties: Additional pinned-license re-fetch failed due to shell network restrictions and raw GitHub web cache misses. Central same-session GitHub license bundles were verified already pinned to the recorded default-branch commit SHA, and complete decoded licenses were read.
Supabase unavailable self-hosting capabilities are managed-platform exclusions, not purchasable self-hosted license unlocks.

Appwrite general self-hosting guide says same features as Cloud, while current Enterprise page explicitly advertises premium self-hosting management features; conservative tier B follows the more specific edition description.
